item.text:
## Finding

1. **Onboarding stops before any capability can be used** — [README.md](/tmp/readme-labs-consumer-repository-guidance-v0.2.0-rc.1/README.md:24), lines 24–39, says to install this plugin and the pinned README Labs release, but gives only the post-install invocation prompts. There is no local-install command, marketplace route, or canonical setup link for either dependency. The repository does identify the plugin as `repository-guidance` in [.codex-plugin/plugin.json](/tmp/readme-labs-consumer-repository-guidance-v0.2.0-rc.1/.codex-plugin/plugin.json:2) and confirms that README review requires the separate `readme-labs` plugin in [upstreams/readme-labs.lock.json](/tmp/readme-labs-consumer-repository-guidance-v0.2.0-rc.1/upstreams/readme-labs.lock.json:9), but neither supplies an install path for a reader.

   A new user therefore cannot reach the README’s main promised result—invoking either owned skill or the separately required README-review skill. Add a concise, maintained installation route for the supported host(s), and explicitly route installation of the pinned README Labs capability.

The evaluation commands, teardown behavior, and internal README links otherwise match the inspected CLI, CI workflow, and evaluation documentation. I did not run live Codex evaluations or verify external GitHub/OpenAI links.
